conventions.axes: Y-up, right-handed; camera looks down -Z by default; ground is the XZ plane at y = 0
conventions.lightIntensity: three.js physical units (directional/hemisphere/ambient: lux-like; spot/point: candela, decay 2)
conventions.easing: named functions from kit/time.js `ease` (formulas in references/kit-api.md)
conventions.camera: fov is vertical field of view in degrees (three.js convention); sensor-agnostic

style.name: Flipbook
style.description: A hand-drawn pencil flipbook riffled under a thumb: a thick pad of cream paper clamped under a walnut bar on a warm, bright desk, most of its pages bent back over the bar in a fan pinched by a stylised thumb. The thumb lets the pages go one at a time; each page curls (real bent-page geometry: hinge angle + bend + corner twist, integrated along the page every frame), falls toward the viewer and slaps flat with a small bounce, so the pencil drawing on the pages comes to life. Every page carries its own procedural graphite drawing from one planner: bold soft-edged lines with graphite grain, light construction circles and arcs, hatching, smudges and a pencil page number, with line boil (each page's strokes wobble by a page-seeded displacement). A real pencil can finish a line on the first page. The release plan gives every flip a paper tick and slap in sync, from a slow page-by-page flip to a full-speed riffle at 12 drawings a second.
motion: Page shape = hinge angle + uniform bend + corner twist, integrated along the page from the binding every frame (closed form of t); never through the stack or the desk.
Held pages fan back over the bar, pinched near one free-edge angle; the inner page slips out first, flicks straight, falls with its free edge lagging, slaps flat and bounces once.
Each page carries its own drawing (page k = drawing k); only the settled top page and the airborne pages get a canvas (pool of 8, slot = k mod 8).
Line boil: every stroke on every page is displaced by a smooth page-seeded wobble, so the drawing shimmers like real hand-drawn animation.

notes.mechanism: riffle.js: release times = explicit slow flips + integrated rate curve; pageState(k,t) = held fan / fall (hinge angle, bend, twist) / bounce / flat; bendPage integrates the angle along each page; drawingFor(k) = the ball->bird story at drawing k with page-seeded line boil.
notes.rate: the riffle runs at 12 pages (drawings) per second — the plan's own number, shown in the label
